newsitem.title: UK: Fedex seeks UK air cargo liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Fedex seeks UK air cargo liberalisation.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said the separation of air cargo services from passenger issues under the UK-U.S. "open skies" talks due to restart on December 4 would improve British trade and exports.

Fedex's chairman, Frederick W. Smith said in a statement on Tuesday, "with bilateral talks about to resume, the UK government should admit that air cargo liberalisation will dramatically improve the trade and export business of British business."
"Liberalisation of cargo services should be separated from the contentious passenger issues at Heathrow airport and seen for what it is, a powerful stimulant to the UK economy," Smith added.

Fedex said its view was supported by a new survey it had commissioned from The Portland Group economic research consultancy to show how improved express cargo services between Britain and the Middle East and Asia could help British business.

The survey showed that lifting the current U.S.-UK bilateral aviation treaty restrictions on air cargo would boost British exports to Asia by 3.1 billion stg a year by providing more direct and efficient access to Asian markets, it added.

UK exporters could gain up to 36 hours lead-time into Asia over their U.S. competitors by faster air cargo express services from Britain, while also cutting their costs by more than 150 million stg annually, the statement said.

Express cargo services, with growth concentrated at regional airports, are not part of the current bilateral debate over access to Heathrow and their door-to- door operations also makes them potential major participants in regional economic development in Britain, Fedex added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
